midnight: The PLA begins a major use of force against Taiwan: an invasion, or a blockade enforced by fire.
summary: Beijing's motive to move early is unchanged since September: warm relations with Washington, a frozen US arms package and a purged high command all still give Xi reasons to wait. What moved is observable pressure. An unannounced deployment of more than 100 ships in early November and coast guard patrols questioning merchant ships east of Taiwan push the preparation layer up, though nothing points to imminent operations. Taiwan's local election results were not in when this was scored. Midnight on this clock is a PLA invasion or a blockade enforced by fire.

dials.assessment: The October plenum expelled 33 Central Committee members, 16 of them PLA generals, after Zhang Youxia and Liu Zhenli were expelled in September. The Central Military Commission is down to Xi and Zhang Shengmin, and no new members were named. The USCC's November report says modernization toward the 2027 goal continues, but the command vacuum is deeper than in September.
dials.name: PLA preparedness

sources.title: AP via WAMC: Zhang Shengmin joins the Politburo

dials.assessment: Q3 2026 GDP grew 4.5%, a little better than Q2's 4.3%, and October exports rose 35% on chip and AI demand. Domestic demand is still weak: October retail sales rose 0.4% and fixed-asset investment is down 8.1% for the year. Weak at home but not in crisis, so still a mild reason for caution.
dials.name: China's struggling economy

sources.title: ING: October data shows fading momentum
AP via KSAT: trade surplus passes $1 trillion

dials.assessment: NCCU's December 2025 survey: 62.0% Taiwanese only, 2.5% Chinese only, 31.7% both. The drift Moore described has plateaued since the 2020 peak of 64.3%. Still a closing window, but it is not accelerating.
dials.name: Taiwan's identity drifting from the mainland

dials.assessment: Births fell 17% to 7.92 million in 2025, the lowest since 1949; population fell 3.39 million, a fourth straight year of decline. The trend is steeper than Moore assumed, though as he notes it bites on a 7 to 20 year horizon, not the next two.
dials.name: China's demographic decline

dials.assessment: TSMC said in October that construction of its second Arizona fab is complete and 3nm volume production is pulled in slightly, to 3Q 2027. TSMC says about 30% of its 2nm-and-below capacity will eventually sit in the US. Taiwan remains irreplaceable today, but the diversification Moore predicted is arriving on roughly his schedule.
dials.name: Importance of Taiwan's chip industry

sources.title: AZ Big Media: TSMC Arizona accelerates timeline

dials.assessment: On Nov 19 a Commerce rule extended US export controls to remote cloud access to advanced chips. China's commerce ministry called it economic coercion and threatened countermeasures, with rare earths the likely lever. The squeeze has tightened a little since September, while China's push for domestic silicon still reduces the pull toward seizing TSMC.
dials.name: Chips' growing importance to China

dials.assessment: The $14B package is still frozen. Reporting before APEC said Washington was weighing a delay until after the APEC and G20 summits, and Trump said after meeting Xi on Nov 19 that he made no commitment on arms. Chinese state media say Trump told Xi the US does not support Taiwan independence, which Washington has not confirmed. Waiting still looks likely to win Beijing more than acting.
dials.name: Growing US commitment to Taiwan

sources.title: Focus Taiwan: Trump on arms sales after Shenzhen
SCMP: US weighs delaying arms sales
Taipei Times: envoy presses on arms package

dials.assessment: The FY26 NDAA authorizes $1B for the Taiwan Security Cooperation Initiative, a Taiwan-contingency interoperability study and Coast Guard training; Taiwanese marines reportedly trained on Guam. The RIMPAC invitation was cut. Integration is growing slowly, so the gap Moore flagged is still open but narrowing.
dials.name: US-Taiwan exercises and interoperability

sources.title: Taiwan Security Monitor on FY26 NDAA

dials.assessment: The Iran war drained US stocks: CNAS cites 53 to 81% of THAAD and 45 to 61% of PAC-3 interceptors expended as of April. In October the Navy signed an SM-6 deal worth about $24B and an SM-3 contract of up to $6.3B, but most FY27 munitions money still depends on reconciliation. China's relative missile advantage remains wide and refilling will take years, though it has stopped widening.
dials.name: China's anti-ship and hypersonic edge

sources.title: CNAS: munitions and the FY27 budget
Atlantic Council: shrinking US missile stocks

dials.assessment: The first Dark Eagle battery began receiving operational missiles in spring 2026, though DOT&E says effectiveness data is insufficient. The Glide Phase Interceptor is unlikely before about 2035. The offensive gap is starting to close; the defensive gap is not.
dials.name: US hypersonic weapons and defenses

dials.assessment: Trump and Xi met for the third time this year at APEC in Shenzhen on Nov 19, with a first Trump-Xi-Putin trilateral, and Xi is expected at the G20 in Miami on Dec 14-15. No tariff deal came out of Shenzhen, and China's pause on rare-earth curbs was extended only to Jan 10, 2027. Relations are warm but the truce is short-dated. Moore's dial says good relations raise the cost of going.
dials.name: State of US-China relations

sources.title: CBS News: Trump, Xi and Putin at APEC

dials.assessment: Xi's APEC speeches stressed cooperation and criticized unilateralism without naming the US, and he called ties stable after meeting Trump. The October plenum communique was inward-looking and did not mention the US. The one hostile note was the commerce ministry's response to the new chip rule. Beijing still appears to see room to get what it wants without force.
dials.name: Xi's view of US intentions

sources.title: Al Jazeera: Xi's pitch at APEC

dials.assessment: Taiwan voted in local elections on Nov 28 and results were not yet published when this was scored. Going in, Lai's approval had recovered to about 52%, the Taipei and New Taipei races had tightened, and KMT chair Cheng Li-wun faced pressure inside her party. Beijing kept up incentives, including a financing deal for Taiwanese firms. The political path Beijing sees through the KMT is still open but looks less certain than in September. Rescore once results are in.
dials.name: Taiwan politics under a DPP government

iw.assessment: October saw 232 PLA aircraft around Taiwan, below the 318 of October 2025, but five joint combat readiness patrols, the most of any month this year. Nov 3 brought 49 sorties in a day, the highest of 2026, and the Liaoning group drilled in the western Pacific. Air activity is still below last year's level, with sharper spikes.
iw.name: PLA air and naval pressure

sources.title: SCMP: naval mobilisation and sortie spike

iw.assessment: Beijing has still not staged a named drill in 2026. In early November, though, Taiwan officials said more than 100 PLA Navy and coast guard ships massed unannounced near Taiwan, in the South China Sea and in the western Pacific, with simulated strikes on Taiwan, on a scale they called larger than Justice Mission 2025. Similar surges were reported in December 2025 and May 2026. Taiwan's defense ministry is watching for a year-end drill.
iw.name: Large-scale drills around Taiwan

sources.title: Reuters via Star-Advertiser: unannounced Pacific drills
SCMP: PLA rehearsing to keep US forces out
Focus Taiwan: MND watching for drills

iw.assessment: The Type 076 Sichuan launched and recovered an autonomous combat aircraft in early November. A Taiwan security official said a drill in Dacheng Bay, Fujian, on Nov 27-28 tested a floating bridge of civilian vessels; that rests on one report. No reporting of ferries being pulled from commercial service or massing at embarkation ports.
iw.name: Amphibious lift and sealift

iw.assessment: China drew on its crude stocks in four of the five months to September as the Hormuz disruption cut imports, then resumed storing in October. Stocks remain very large, and soybean imports are being held at ports because of a domestic glut. The reserve is still a warning indicator, but this autumn it was being used, not built.
iw.name: Strategic stockpiling

sources.title: Reuters column: China resumes storing crude
Reuters column: China uses crude stockpiles

iw.assessment: On Oct 18 Taiwan drove off 16 Chinese vessels working four areas at once, and its coast guard says militia boats now operate with coast guard ships. In early November a China Coast Guard patrol east of Taiwan radioed merchant ships for port and crew details, and China claimed to have inspected 198 vessels. No physical boarding has been reported. This is a step along the path a quarantine would take.
iw.name: Coast guard and gray-zone moves

sources.title: Al Jazeera: Taiwan drives away 16 Chinese ships
Taipei Times: coast guard queries merchant ships
Taipei Times: militia and coast guard

iw.assessment: No open-source reporting found of unusual reservist call-ups, blood drives, recruitment surges, travel restrictions on PLA personnel, or advisories pulling PRC nationals out of Taiwan or allied countries. The search this round was in English only.
iw.name: Domestic mobilization signals

iw.assessment: Xi said on Nov 12 that reunification must and will be realized, without mentioning force; Taiwan's Mainland Affairs Council judged it consistent with past positions. Beijing marked Taiwan Recovery Day on Oct 25 and pressed Trump on Taiwan at Shenzhen. No new legal instruments tied to Taiwan this quarter.
iw.name: Rhetoric and legal groundwork

factors.name: A 'sacred commitment' to Taiwan
factors.note: Unchanged. Beijing's readouts from both 2026 summits frame Taiwan as central to national reunification and territorial integrity.

factors.name: Authoritarian decision-making risk
factors.note: The October plenum expelled 16 more generals and left the Central Military Commission as Xi plus one. Fewer officers can give Xi candid readiness assessments. This cuts both ways: less capability, more risk of miscalculation.

factors.name: Xi's political incentive
factors.note: The October plenum set the 21st Party Congress for the second half of 2027, and analysts expect Xi to take a fourth term with no heir named. Taiwan remains the legacy prize, though summit diplomacy now offers Xi visible wins without war.

sources.title: Focus Taiwan: plenum sets the congress
Foreign Policy: who will succeed Xi

factors.name: PLA readiness goal for 2027
factors.note: The 2027 goal still stands as a capability marker. The USCC's November report says modernization toward it continues despite the purges, while the 2026 ODNI assessment sees no fixed timetable and other analysts judge the purges put it out of reach.

history.note: Moore's published reading. He judged an invasion likely within one to three years.
Baseline. Relations warmed after two summits; arms package frozen; PLA leadership purged; US munitions depleted by the Iran war.
Preparation layer up: an unannounced 100-ship deployment in early November and coast guard patrols questioning merchant ships east of Taiwan. Dials unchanged; election results pending.
